text:
Detroit arrives at Vancouver two days removed from a 4-3 shootout loss at SEA, where Alex DeBrincat reached 300 career goals. The Red Wings are 2-0-3 in their last five and are missing J.T. Compher, Mason Appleton and Marco Kasper. The Canucks are in a much darker place: winless in eight (0-7-1), outscored 36-16 in that stretch, and coming off a 6-3 home loss to CAR. The chances say the slump is real. VAN has taken only 40% of the expected goals (the quality of chances created) at five on five this season, and 35% during the skid.

Detroit has controlled more of the play, 51% at five on five, but it's also taking 4.7 penalties a game. That matters against a Vancouver penalty kill that ranks 30th in chances allowed, facing a DET power play that ranks fifth in chances created. In net, projected starter John Gibson sits at -1.7 goals saved above expected (how many goals a goalie stopped compared with what his shots deserved) this season, and was +10.11 last year. Projected Canucks starter Kevin Lankinen is at -11.28 this season and -20.31 last.

For Detroit, DeBrincat is 46% to score tonight, and Dylan Larkin is 38%. Ice Sheet's under-the-radar pick is Michael Brandsegg-Nygård, a third-liner with 3.7 expected goals in his last nine games. For Vancouver, Brock Boeser has a four-game point streak and is 56% for a point.
